title: On Wasting two whole days waiting
subtitle: 习惯自律 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）
meta: 主题语境：习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）　|　核心词汇：waste　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 waste 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1980 the cook ① wasted two whole days waiting before dawn, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② wastes two whole days waiting in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ waste two whole days waiting at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ wasted two whole days waiting before — a line in the menu for September 1974 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Wasting two whole days waiting before dawn, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ waste no time over small talk in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Waste no time over small talk at once and never mention it again.

By 1987 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ wastes no time over small talk before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ wasted two whole days waiting again when nobody else would.

⑩ To waste two whole days waiting, my mother said in 1992, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody wastes two whole days waiting in public again and somebody must waste two whole days waiting before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 浪费（一般过去式 wasted two whole days waiting：1980 年厨子头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 浪费（一般现在 wastes two whole days waiting：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 浪费（不定式 to waste two whole days waiting：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 浪费（过去完成时 had wasted two whole days waiting：1974 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 浪费（动名词 wasting two whole days waiting 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 虚度（waste no time over small talk：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去虚度不在闲话上浪费时间）
G. v. 虚度（waste no time over small talk：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 浪费（后段两处：新来的客人照例 wastes no time over small talk，而母亲又一次 wasted two whole days waiting）

items.q: to waste two whole days waiting
wasted two whole days waiting before
waste no time over small talk in public
waste no time over small talk at once
wastes no time over small talk before dawn
wasted two whole days waiting again
to waste two whole days waiting

answers.why: waste 意为“浪费”，1980 年厨子天没亮就浪费整整两天耗在等待上，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 wasted。
waste 意为“浪费”，自那以后厨子当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 wastes。
waste 意为“浪费”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯浪费整整两天耗在等待上”，此处为不定式 to waste two whole days waiting。
waste 意为“浪费”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1987 年之前就有人浪费过，故用过去完成时 had wasted。
waste 意为“浪费”，厨子说“浪费整整两天耗在等待上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 wasting two whole days waiting 作主语。
waste 意为“虚度”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去虚度不在闲话上浪费时间”，should ever 之后用原形 waste no time over small talk。
waste 意为“虚度”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻虚度不在闲话上浪费时间（waste no time over small talk at once），以后再也不要提起。
waste 意为“浪费”，新来的客人每个日子都照例虚度不在闲话上浪费时间，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 wastes。
waste 意为“浪费”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就浪费整整两天耗在等待上，用一般过去式 wasted 叙述。
waste 意为“浪费”，结尾那句是母亲 1992 年的话：要浪费整整两天耗在等待上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

多年以后，厨子仍当着众人面做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（wastes two whole days waiting）

厨子说过，天没亮就浪费整整两天耗在等待上这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（wasting two whole days waiting 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻虚度不在闲话上浪费时间，以后再也不要提起。（waste no time over small talk，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 waste 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1980 the cook wasted two whole days waiting before dawn, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook wastes two whole days waiting in public whenever the canteen asks.
Wasting two whole days waiting before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever waste no time over small talk in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen wastes no time over small talk before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother wasted two whole days waiting again, and the canteen remembered that half.
